title: Define SLO-backed Dedicated throughput commitments, error-budget policy, and contract language
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: produce a single canonical specification and contract snippet the Sales + Legal teams can use when promising Dedicated throughput guarantees to customers. This ticket defines (1) precise SLOs and measurement windows for committed throughput, (2) an error-budget policy and burn / remediation playbook, (3) transparent crediting/billing adjustment formula, and (4) monitoring/telemetry queries and owner responsibilities. Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity often need deterministic throughput for production features (e.g., live chat at scale, synchronous embeddings pipelines). Existing contract drafts are inconsistent about how throughput is measured (peak vs rolling average), how maintenance/upgrade windows are handled, and how credits are calculated. Goals: - Make throughput commitments measurable and auditable with existing telemetry. - Limit legal ambiguity by providing simple, customer-friendly credit formulas. - Provide clear escalation/remediation actions before crediting. - Define how autoscaling and burst policies interact with guaranteed baseline capacity. Scope and non-goals: - Scope includes on-hosted Redwood-managed Dedicated pools. Does not include Private on-prem installs (separate legal/ops considerations). - This ticket proposes language for contract exhibits and an operational runbook; it does not implement runtime instrumentation (ENG tickets will follow).
acceptance_criteria: A clear SLO statement for Dedicated throughput committed as a rolling 30-day effective throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) and an availability metric covering configuration and scheduling failures.
A defensible measurement method using existing telemetry (per-customer routing counts, model variant mapping, node health) with query examples that engineering can implement.
A documented error-budget policy that specifies when remediation is triggered, what automated mitigations run, and when credits are issued.
A short contract exhibit (<= 250 words) for Sales/Legal describing credits and customer obligations (e.g., providing request traces) that legal can drop into MSA/Order Form.
Runbook steps and owner list that map to existing on-call rotations for SRE/Capacity and Product ops for the first-ditch response.
Sign-off from Legal, Sales engineering, and SRE before moving to Done.
Dependencies (ENG) created: implement measurement queries and a daily SLO dashboard for customer-facing reporting.
proposed_contract_language: Throughput Commitment. Vendor agrees to provide Customer with a baseline Dedicated throughput equal to the Committed Throughput specified in the Order Form. Committed Throughput is measured as the 30-day rolling average of successful service completions (tokens/sec) routed to Vendor-managed Dedicated capacity for Customer account(s).

Service Measurement and Exclusions. Measurement is computed from Vendor telemetry and excludes (a) Customer-induced errors (as defined in Exhibit A), (b) scheduled maintenance windows notified at least 72 hours in advance, and (c) force-majeure events. Vendor will provide a daily report of measured throughput on request.

Remediation and Credits. If Measured Throughput over a billing period falls below 99% of Committed Throughput for a given 30-day window and the Shortfall Duration exceeds 60 cumulative minutes in that window, Customer will receive a credit applied to the next invoice equal to: Credit = Invoice Amount * min(0.25, ShortfallPercent * 0.5). ShortfallPercent = (CommittedThroughput - EffectiveThroughput) / CommittedThroughput. Credits are capped at 25% of the monthly fee for the affected capacity line item.

Grace Capacity and Bursts. Vendor may offer configured burst capacity for short-lived peaks. Burst capacity is not included in Committed Throughput calculations unless explicitly purchased and listed in the Order Form.

Customer Cooperation. To investigate potential throughput issues, Customer must provide request traces and sample payloads when requested. Failure to provide cooperation within 5 business days may delay remediation and credit eligibility.
measurement_method: Primary metric: per-customer successful token completions per second aggregated across Dedicated nodes. Compute 30-day rolling average sampled at 1-minute resolution. Use rolling percentiles for latency and a separate node-health availability measure. Exclude scheduled maintenance (window tags) and spikes from non-routed test traffic. Measurement owner: Capacity Engineering (ENG-capacity).
credit_formula: If 30-day EffectiveThroughput < 0.99 * CommittedThroughput and cumulative minutes below threshold > 60, then Credit = min(0.25 * MonthlyFee, MonthlyFee * ShortfallPercent * 0.5). Apply credit only to the Dedicated capacity line item. Legal to confirm rounding rules.
error_budget_policy: Error budget is tracked on a rolling 30-day window. Budget depletion triggers: - Warning alert at 50% depletion: capacity on-call reviews autoscaling and scheduling configs. - Action alert at 80% depletion: trigger targeted remediation runbook (see Runbook steps). - Critical at 95% depletion: begin customer communication plan and prepare credit calculation. Budget burn sources: autoscaling failures, node scheduling collisions, model variant mismatches, networking throttles. Maintenance adjustments: scheduled maintenance subtracts from the rolling window as excluded only if announced per contract terms.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: Capacity on-call pulls latest 30-day throughput trend dashboard and checks node health for Dedicated pool (5 min)
2) Determine cause class: (a) capacity saturation, (b) scheduler placement failure, (c) model variant fallback causing slower tokens/sec, (d) infra/networking issues (15 min)
3) Immediate mitigation: increase autoscaling target by X% (if safe), temporarily divert non-critical traffic, enable hot-cache priming for KV cache (30 min)
4) Communicate: Post status to customer channel and internal #dedicated-capacity incident thread (within 60 min)
5) Postmortem: document root cause, duration, and whether credit threshold was met, attach telemetry and remediation steps (5 days)
6) Prevent recurrence: schedule follow-up ENG task(s) if systemic (capacity tuning, kernel scheduling changes, or console alert tuning).
risks: Measurement mismatch: customers may send traffic through multiple routes or proxies; must ensure vendor telemetry captures only billed flows.
Credit unpredictability: overly generous credits could expose financial risk; caps added to mitigate.
Operational friction: requiring customer traces may be a barrier to swift remediation; limit requirement to reasonable samples and define PII sanitation process.
Autoscaling interactions: automatic scale-ups that draw from a shared pool could mask true Dedicated capacity issues; policy must clearly define isolation guarantees.
rollout_plan: Week 0: Align with Legal and Sales on proposed contract exhibit and cap language.
Week 1: ENG implements measurement queries and daily SLO dashboard for beta customers.
Week 2: Run SLA simulation with 2 pilot customers and validate telemetry and credit calculations.
Week 3: Gather feedback, finalize contract wording, and publish to Sales playbook.
Week 4: Enable generally for new Dedicated orders; grandfather existing contracts per renewal terms.
